The '''NI USRP-2954R''' is the SDR platform used for the IHF OFDM-based JCAS project. The device contains two RF channels implemented with two UBX-160 daughterboards and connects to the host through two 10 Gigabit Ethernet links.

Use the current NI specification sheet for formal limits and measurement conditions.

== RF connectors and channel mapping ==

Each UBX-160 daughterboard transmits through <code>TX/RX</code> and receives through either <code>TX/RX</code> or <code>RX2</code>. Full-duplex operation on one daughterboard forces reception through <code>RX2</code>.

UHD channel numbers, physical daughterboards, RF connectors, and SFP+ Ethernet ports are separate concepts. Record the mapping reported by UHD for every test; do not infer it from an IP address or cable position.

== Startup checks ==

Check both network interfaces before starting GNU Radio. Replace the interface placeholders with the names reported by the host.

<pre>
ip -br address
ip -s link show &lt;interface-30&gt;
ip -s link show &lt;interface-40&gt;
sudo ethtool &lt;interface-30&gt;
sudo ethtool &lt;interface-40&gt;

sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.wmem_max

ping -c 4 192.168.30.2
ping -c 4 192.168.40.2

uhd_find_devices
uhd_usrp_probe \
  --args="type=x300,addr=192.168.30.2,second_addr=192.168.40.2"
</pre>

Confirm that both links operate at 10 Gbit/s with MTU 9000, both daughterboards are detected, the FPGA image is compatible with UHD, and no LO or device errors are reported.

== FPGA image ==

The XG image is required when both SFP+ ports are used at 10 Gigabit Ethernet. Reflash only for initial setup, recovery, or an intentional image change, then power-cycle the USRP.

<pre>
uhd_image_loader --args="type=x300,addr=192.168.30.2,fpga=XG"
</pre>

== GNU Radio use ==

Use a UHD USRP Source for reception and a UHD USRP Sink for transmission. A hardware source or sink controls the data rate, so do not add a Throttle block to a hardware-connected flowgraph.

For reproducible measurements, record:

* USRP, motherboard, and daughterboard serial numbers;
* UHD, GNU Radio, and FPGA image versions;
* requested and actual clock, sample rate, center frequency, gain, and analog bandwidth;
* CPU and over-the-wire sample formats;
* channel, daughterboard, antenna connector, and LO-lock state; and
* overruns, underruns, timeouts, tune coercion, and other warnings.

== RF safety ==

* Carry out conducted checks without antennas and disable RF output before changing connections.
* Use rated 50-ohm terminations, cables, adapters, and attenuators.
* Never apply more than -15 dBm to a receiver input. The JCAS receiver characterization uses -20 dBm as a conservative test ceiling.
* Start generator and transmitter tests at low power and increase the level only while the complete signal path remains within its ratings.
* Do not connect a transmitter directly to a receiver without verified attenuation and isolation.

== Troubleshooting ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Symptom
! Checks
|-
| USRP not found
| Check link state, host subnet, ping response, firewall settings, and the address arguments passed to UHD.
|-
| Compatibility or FPGA error
| Verify the installed UHD version and the FPGA image, then reload the matching image if required.
|-
| Overruns or underruns
| Check both 10 Gigabit Ethernet links, MTU, socket buffers, actual sample rate, CPU load, and sample formats.
|-
| Unexpected RF frequency or level
| Record requested and actual tune values, LO lock, connector selection, gain, analog bandwidth, correction state, and external path loss.
|}
